On-disk dtype records

Source: R/dtype.R
dtype-records.Rd

Internal mechanism that keeps the On-disk dtype of numeric Elements that R cannot represent natively (float32, int8, int16, the unsigned integers, int64 and the sparse index dtypes).

Usage

get_dtype(x)

set_dtype(x, dtype)

drop_dtype(x)

get_nullable(x)

set_nullable(x, na_value = TRUE)

check_dtype_fits(x, dtype, path, call = rlang::caller_env())

write_dtype(x, path, call = rlang::caller_env())

sparse_write_dtypes(x, path, call = rlang::caller_env())

read_dataset(loc, name, selection = NULL, call = rlang::caller_env())

write_dataset(
  loc,
  name,
  x,
  scalar = FALSE,
  dataset_kwargs = list(),
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

Arguments

x

A numeric value.

dtype

A dtype name from numeric_dtypes.

path

Path of the Element, used in errors.

call

The call reported by errors.

loc

An open rhdf5 file or group handle.

name

Name or path of a dataset below loc.

selection

A selection of the array to read, see io-store.

scalar

Whether to write a scalar dataspace.

dataset_kwargs

A list of dataset creation options, see io-compression.

Details

The record is the anndata_dtype attribute (see anndata-matrix-values). Dense values hold a single dtype name such as "float32". Sparse matrices hold a named character vector with the names data, indices and indptr. Plain vectors and arrays that carry a record also get the S3 class anndata_typed, whose print method hides the attribute, so they print and compute like ordinary R values. Subsetting, copy and transpose copy the record with copy_dtype().

The nullable record is the anndata_nullable attribute, set by the readers of nullable-integer, nullable-boolean and nullable-string-array. It makes the value write back as a nullable Element even when it holds no NA, as Python writes any pandas nullable array. For strings it holds the na-value attribute ("NaN" or "NA"), and it is TRUE for the other types.

Reading with read_dataset() records the dtype only where it differs from the R type returned, which is float64 for double and int32 for integer. Writing with write_dataset() restores the recorded dtype, or the R type when there is no record, and raises anndata_dtype_overflow_error when the values no longer fit. It never truncates or wraps.

int64 and uint64 are read as double when every value has magnitude below 2^53 and otherwise raise anndata_dtype_overflow_error. An int32 dataset holding -2147483648, the bit pattern of NA_integer_, is read as double with an int32 record.
